newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania to offer bank, gas firm for sale.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania to offer bank, gas firm for sale.

text.p: The Lithuanian government said on Thursday that it had agreed with the World Bank that it would privatise two state banks, the state gas company and a state-owned oil company.
"The World Bank positively evaluated the privatisation plan of the banks, which should be approved on February 28," the government press office said in a statement.
The statement said the government intended to privatise the State Commercial Bank and the Agricultural Bank.
The World Bank had pushed Lithuania to sell its remaining state banks as part of agreements to gain World Bank credits.
It also said that with the help of international financial advisors it would draw up a plan to privatise Lithuanian Gas and its subsidiaries.
It said that a similar method would be used for privatising companies in the oil sector.
Lithuania plans to merge its four oil sector companies into one large enterprise, to be called Lithuanian Oil.
The government said that it expected a further $40 million in World Bank credits in the spring after receiving a first tranche of $40 million in September 1996.
The statement also said that the energy sector will be decentralized and realistic electricity, gas and heating prices would be established.
Lithuania's energy sector is caught in a vicious circle of debt, with consumers unable to pay producers even at subsidised prices and producers in turn failing to pay their suppliers.
"This government is ready to carry out rapid, systematic and structural reforms to the country's economy," the statement quoted Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius as saying.
